title: Crop Establishment
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Prepare three small plots side by side: fine (carrots), medium (beans or maize) and coarse (sweet potato vines or arrowroot). Use jembes, forked jembes and rakes with the teacher's rules for carrying tools.

skills.key_step: The child matches the tilth to the planting material: fine for small seeds (carrot, onion), medium for medium seeds (maize, beans), coarse for large materials (tubers, vines, suckers, cuttings), and says why.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to make a fine seedbed.
floor.question: Why break the soil fine for tiny seeds?

steps: Look at the size of the planting material.
Small: fine. Medium: medium. Large: coarse.

board.do: Draw a carrot seed, a bean and a sweet potato vine.
Write fine, medium, coarse under each.

misconceptions.ask: Which tilth suits small seeds like carrot?
misconceptions.repair: Sow carrot seed on a lumpy tray and a fine tray; count how many come up.

misconceptions.ask: Which tilth suits sweet potato cuttings?
misconceptions.repair: Explain that big planting materials need air and loose clods; fine soil packs hard round them.

misconceptions.ask: Which tilth suits maize and beans?
misconceptions.repair: Lay carrot, bean and potato side by side: small, medium, large match fine, medium, coarse.
Show three trays of the same soil dug to different sizes.

skills.key_step: The child says how a seedbed is prepared to the right tilth: clear, dig (primary cultivation) when moist, remove roots and stones, break clods (secondary cultivation) to fine, medium or coarse, level and rake for small seeds.

floor.prerequisite: Knows which tilth suits which planting material.
floor.question: Which tilth for carrots?

steps: Break clods to the tilth needed; level and rake for small seeds.

board.do: Write the cards: rake, dig, clear.

misconceptions.ask: Which is done first when preparing a seedbed?
misconceptions.repair: Try to rake a hard, uncleared plot.

listen_for: When the soil is soaking wet
misconceptions.ask: When is the best time to dig a seedbed?
misconceptions.repair: Dig a lump of soaked clay: it smears and dries into hard clods.

misconceptions.ask: Why are weed roots removed when preparing a seedbed?
misconceptions.repair: Show couch grass roots sprouting from a small piece.

misconceptions.ask: Which tool is used to dig hard ground first?
misconceptions.repair: Show each tool and what it does to a lump of hard soil.

checks.question: Which tool is used for primary cultivation?
Why not dig soaking wet soil?
checks.answer: it smears and dries into hard clods
